does: Interval/sign/null abstract interpretation, widening and bounds diagnostics.
consumer: NF_BOUNDS_PROVEN is written but not read by AIR/PEAR. No bounds-elision or LLVM range-attribute consumer.
limits: Analysis works; the backend-effect comment overstates integration.

does: Feature census and convention audit over the AST.
consumer: Reporting/convention diagnostics; feature presence does not actually gate all pipeline allocations/walks.
limits: Not a compiler or backend for the advertised constructs.

does: Bounded symbolic path simulation and contradiction diagnostics.
consumer: Reports/warnings; no production LLVM symbolic execution, proof-guided rewrite or emitted path constraints.
limits: Bounded syntactic model, not an SMT-backed universal verifier.

does: Structural tree checks and before/after aggregate snapshots.
consumer: Can reject malformed transformed trees with E3270; snapshot reports counts.
limits: Eight structural invariants do not establish semantics/effect/type-metadata preservation; one snapshot pair does not identify a particular pass.

does: Builds/contracts a separate CPS term representation and identifies tail calls.
consumer: CPS dump and tail diagnostics; NF_TAIL feeds auxiliary continuation analysis, not LLVM tail-call lowering.
limits: The native emitter does not consume this CPS IR.

does: Tracks handlers, performed operations, resume positions and continuation leaks.
consumer: Diagnostics and NF_TAIL on arms.
limits: No runtime prompt/capture/resume machinery is generated from its representation.

does: Handler coverage, effect rows, row discharge and generic-instantiation census.
consumer: Checks/reports; contributes theory-only models.
limits: The Monomorphiser census is not body specialization or a runtime handler implementation.

does: Ownership/use/move and borrowing-oriented AST/path checks.
consumer: Source diagnostics, not automatic allocation/free or general linear-runtime enforcement.
limits: Heuristic/budgeted analysis; do not equate its checks with a borrow-checker proof for all programs.

does: Poison/UB/frozen/taint-oriented source analysis.
consumer: Diagnostics/census; native freeze/safety semantics do not follow from the counters.
limits: Separate from PEAR trap lowering and LLVM poison semantics.

does: Real module CFG plus reaching defs, available expressions, very-busy expressions and live-variable solvers.
consumer: Internal fact tables, certificates and report only.
limits: No AIR/PEAR input or optimizer consumer of DfBundle results found. The algorithms are not merely fake counters, but their solved facts are disconnected.

does: Closure free-variable/escape analysis and capture hazards.
consumer: NF_ADDR_TAKEN affects later NbE/CRDT; NF_NOESCAPE has no operational reader outside its writers/dump.
limits: No emitted closure tags, dispatch or mutable-capture boxing. Backend-consumer comments are too broad.

does: Registers opcode names and rejects unknown names; also implements a lowering-table algorithm and PGL matrix builder.
consumer: Validation is live. add_lowering has no call site; all registered op.rule_count stay zero, making lower_tree a production no-op.
limits: Arity remains unknown too: opcode registration sets arity_known=false and only the unused add_lowering can set it. A registry is not a working MLIR-style lowering pipeline.

does: IRDL constraint-variable operations and union-find verification model.
consumer: Auxiliary dialect constraint reports.
limits: Neither this SSA-like constraint graph nor a full IRDL type schema becomes native compiler IR.

does: Checks declared dialect traits against source AST structures.
consumer: Diagnostics, some strict-mode enforcement.
limits: Trait verification is not opcode implementation or backend instruction selection.

does: Builds a per-function CFG and solves liveness/nonlocal classifications.
consumer: theory_opt reads its vars table for a conservative dead-local check.
limits: Not the LLVM SSA representation; retained state/dump is last-function oriented, and the consumer uses uses/address/nonlocal conditions rather than a general interprocedural analysis.

does: Builds an auxiliary decision DAG and identifies a validated dense scalar dispatch subset.
consumer: In PR: NF_DENSE_SWITCH reaches AIR and actual LLVM switch creation; raw-IR probe has 3 switches on versus 0 off.
limits: Current dev has no such backend wiring. Full decision DAG is not consumed by PEAR; enum payload/guard/general matching remain partial.

does: Checks pattern reachability/exhaustiveness and counterexamples; writes NF_EXHAUSTIVE.
consumer: Diagnostics; flow code reads NF_EXHAUSTIVE but runs before this theory write.
limits: Do not treat that earlier flow reader as evidence the later theory flag is consumed in this run. Full pattern certificates do not implement runtime destructuring.

does: Real CFG, dominance/frontier and SSA/phi construction in its own graph.
consumer: Dump/report only.
limits: No AIR/PEAR consumer. Native SSA largely comes from LLVM over separately emitted allocas, not this graph.

does: Contextual modal/staging judgments and quote/context consistency.
consumer: Source checks/reports.
limits: Not a full elaborating dependent/contextual type system or native code quotation runtime.

does: Provides context/substitution storage APIs; production scan only recursively walks children and absorb copies hereditary counters.
consumer: Report via HeredState metadata/counters.
limits: Source explicitly states it does not solve meta-variables or run contextual occurs-checks; those counts remain zero.

does: Translates source to auxiliary typed terms, normalizes by hereditary substitution and issues judgments/notes.
consumer: Feeds MetaCtx and diagnostics.
limits: Normalized units are not reified onto the production AST for native compilation. Do not confuse this with the separate mutating theory_nbe.

does: Scoped-effect registry, normalized continuation-tree model, UB tracker and structural subtype cache.
consumer: Bidi/checks use the cache; continuation tree is retained/reported.
limits: No continuation-tree consumer in AIR/PEAR or generated HOSE runtime. Models can run without implementing native effects.

does: Checks quote/splice stage levels, variable escapes and quote interning.
consumer: Real hard errors E3201/E3202, plus stage metadata.
limits: Checks stage soundness; does not by itself execute code generators or emit quoted code at runtime.

does: Mutates source AST for a restricted lambda fragment: beta/delta/eta, immutable values, evaluation-order guards and capture avoidance.
consumer: Returned/updated AST reaches AIR.
limits: Real runtime enabler: simple and higher-order lambda probes return 42 on, segfault off. Bounded subset, not all higher-order functions/escaping closures.

does: Unifies generic signatures, solves substitutions and makes monomorphic signatures.
consumer: Only fallback write is call.type_slot when the primary inferencer left it null.
limits: No specialized source bodies or emitted monomorphized LLVM functions. Mostly signatures/checks/reports, not full code specialization.

does: Approximates function side effects and parameter write/escape sets.
consumer: CRDT consumes NF_PURE_FN; PR maps it to memory(read) and maps NF_READONLY_PARAM to captures(none).
limits: The consumer is real, but producer escape analysis misses assignment-RHS storage, demonstrated by address bits stored under captures(none). Heap reads are called mathematically pure in diagnostics; noalias/read-only advice also overreaches.

does: Partial evaluation/residualization, forced comptime evaluation and bounded static-loop unrolling.
consumer: Production AST replacement.
limits: Comptime probe returns 42 on versus 0 off. Scalar evaluator and supported constructs are bounded; metadata transfer is not covered by the clone/egraph selftest.

does: Structural equality/hash-consing, clone and pattern substitution helpers.
consumer: Used by rewriting/other theory models; cloned nodes reach production transforms.
limits: Hash-consing alone is not optimization. Metadata preservation differs between clone and other fresh-node/substitution paths.

does: Effect footprints, commutativity, independence and reduction classification.
consumer: Uses qualifier facts; writes NF_INDEPENDENT/NF_REDUCTION.
limits: No operational readers for those output flags; no statement scheduling, parallelization or reduction-code generation.

does: E-class constant/lattice analysis attached to equality saturation.
consumer: Can inject/evaluate constants within the saturator at explicit rewrite sites.
limits: Not a general runtime abstract interpreter or arbitrary-source optimization pass.

does: Equality saturation and cost extraction with source metadata preservation.
consumer: Used by RwSites for explicit fixpoint rewrites, then replaces the AST subject.
limits: Not globally applied to all arithmetic; axioms are supplied rules, not a proof that each rule preserves arbitrary effects or language semantics.

does: AST constant/algebra/branch folding, DCE/copy propagation and block flattening.
consumer: Mutated AST reaches AIR; limited liveness consumer.
limits: CSE is a census plus NF_USED mark, not expression substitution. Much simple optimization overlaps primary constfold/SCCP and LLVM. Calls are conservatively not considered pure here.

does: Evaluates scoped rewrite values/composition and replaces explicit pipeline/fixpoint sites.
consumer: Actual source AST replacement with TRS/egraph results.
limits: Corrected explicit rewrite probe changes native result to 42. Rules do not apply everywhere just because they were declared.

does: Pattern/guard substitution, ordered rewriting and fuel-bounded fixpoint evaluation.
consumer: RwSites invokes it on the requested subject.
limits: Supported patterns/guards and finite fuel; termination/confluence are separate analyses, not a universal semantic-preservation proof.

does: LPO termination/critical-pair/confluence analysis of a rule set.
consumer: RwSites invokes RuleSet.analyse; same C3 namespace as theory_trs.
limits: Real proof-model work on used rule sets; conclusions are bounded/syntax-specific, not validation of arbitrary optimization equations.

does: Allocates, initializes and sequences theory passes and a gradual-sort checker.
consumer: Root AST is returned to driver; checks can change acceptance, transforms/facts reach later stages.
limits: Runs only entry AST and under the driver verify guard. Pass count counts invocations, not useful work or proven program properties. CPU clock is labeled wall timing.

does: Bidirectional modal-type synthesis/checking over a separate type store.
consumer: Diagnostics, strict settings, type-model reports.
limits: Not the production TypeTable checker or a replacement for its universal typing/ABI rules.

does: Recursive-type translation, contractivity/inhabitation/coinductive shape checks.
consumer: Uses shared theoretical TypeStore and emits diagnostics.
limits: No recursive-layout/native-type codegen from MuState. Separate from primary type mapping.

does: Typed record rows, width/depth/formula relations and TypeStore materialization.
consumer: Internal relation/formula checks and large built-in semantic-law audit.
limits: No backend record-layout consumer; 70+ field analysis succeeding does not fix PEAR 16-field runtime limitations. Built-in laws run even with zero source structs.

does: Principal-row/effect constraints and inference in a separate model.
consumer: Checks/reports.
limits: No native handler specialization or universal compiler effect enforcement from those rows.

does: Size-change matrices/closure and termination classification with budgets.
consumer: Notes/warnings; no LLVM willreturn/mustprogress consumer from SCT.
limits: Cannot promote its reported termination proof to a native attribute without a specified supported fragment and soundness checks.

does: Session-store/coinductive duality plus source-name/operation matching and endpoint-use checks.
consumer: Diagnostics/reporting for recognized channel APIs.
limits: No session/channel runtime codegen or universal deadlock-freedom guarantee for the compiled program.

does: TypeStore, primitive/Boolean constructors, owned record entries and algebra operations.
consumer: Shared by mu/record/subtype theory models and engine.
limits: A type-model store, not LLVM types or runtime value representation; bounded capacities.

does: Type-dependency SCC/alias-cycle/guardedness/regularity checks.
consumer: Alias cycles really reject with E4240; NF_RECURSIVE_TY only analysis/dump.
limits: The flag does not drive recursive native layout; nominal/type-policy coverage is limited.

does: Bounded DNF/semantic subtype model and production match/alias/binding advice bridge.
consumer: In PR attaches the real engine to supported set-algebra emptiness checks; W3291/W3292 are lint-only.
limits: Not the universal primary subtype rule. Syntactic has_set_operator filter skips direct named-alias bindings even when the alias itself is proven empty.

does: Three-valued, budgeted structural/set-theoretic subtype/emptiness procedure.
consumer: 47-case standalone selftest; PR MatchRefiner queries for narrow emptiness advice.
limits: Current dev only standalone selftest path, not the new production bridge. A passing selftest is not a program-wide type-safety proof.

does: A separate recursive semantic-type/emptiness engine plus extensive law audits.
consumer: Record model uses it for relation checks and built-in audit examples.
limits: Distinct semantics/stores from the primary checker and 47-case engine; not a universal native compiler checker.
